It’s 2026 and after many years of experiencing the 'EA' treatment with their games, I honestly didn’t think they could surprise me anymore, but man, was I wrong...

PAYWALLING the tutorial island is beyond a joke. Not only did it take six months after early access to make it available again, because the main island is boring and repetitive, now you want people to pay just to teleport to an area every single person playing this game has already experienced, unbelievable.

After dedicating myself to beating the first season pass I was rewarded with very little incentive to play because I'll only keep a "portion of my premium currency" when the second season arrives. My silly efforts to do the same in the second season have been justly rewarded with the "incentive" being completely removed upon the arrival of the new season, namely any of the season pass currency you earned (or paid for if you were REALLY stupid) not being carried over. To explain, the latest update to the purchasable/earnable currency used to earn items and unlock new pages in the battlepass's will auto-spend at the end of each season, going from a system that let you retain SOME semblance of reward for your previous playtime, into a new one that essentially says to the player: "Oh? you were saving your currency for stuff that isn't this garbage? What a shame, we just bought it all for you. No, you can't keep the change. No, I don't care that you spent real money on it. You can have some more worthless AI-generated crap if you give me $10 though." 

Are you guys being held at gunpoint or something? You're sat on one of the most fluid and satisfying skate games ever made and you seem intent on making everyone who enjoys playing it feel like an imbecile for giving it more than a moment of their time. I enjoy playing this game. I want to support it. Please give me a single reason to.

I installed the game and tried to launch it
it got an error involving Javelin Anticheat, It asked me to get rid of some old driver
so I did and tried launching it again. This went on for several minutes of issues....
I removed every program it asked me to, until it demanded I remove the driver for my wireless headset (Corsair iCUE), which I am absolutely certain shouldn't be an issue.

At that point, I knew it was a hard "no" for me, but I uninstalled iCUE temporarily
just to see if the game would start....

i restarted my PC and tried launching the game again
it then showed an error regarding my GPU's fan control software...
and immediately after that, i got a Blue Screen of Death

All this hassle just to run a skateboarding game...
I uninstalled the game immediately after all that.

I spoke to a friend who said he had encountered similar errors
(except for the Blue Screen), and he gave up on the game too.

I googled to understand why Javelin is so aggressive towards absolutely everything installed on the PC...
And to my lack of surprise I discovered that Javelin operates at the Windows kernel level and likely has more system privileges than even you, the Administrator, do.

Not only is that way too much especially for the game in question
but it also ensures I will never launch a game with this anticheat again.
I will never buy or play anything that uses this system.
It’s disappointing, especially considering this was a specific game I really wanted to play.

The use of anti-cheat software is understandable,
but there’s a limit to how intrusive these things should be on a user's computer.

After dealing with a Blue Screen of Death and spending minutes uninstalling a bunch of drivers/programs only to find out that the next time I launch, it’s going to take issue with some other random stupid program that has nothing to do with cheating
I never want to go near a game that uses this Javelin system, never again.

This is my first ever skating game, so I have no connection to the other skates or other skating IPs. 

But I do hate this game and here is why: 

-EA is the publisher (no more needs to be said about that)

-Always online... WHY?? Why cant we just have a single player skating game that has a multiplayer lobby?? How does always being online make the game better??

-Buggy azz mess that seems to get worse over time the more you play. The stuttering 20 min into skating is  frustrating, especially when you try to get challenges done. I cant even do a simple kickflip without the jankyness. Dont let your player bump anything because then they will dramatically ragdoll (which would be funny if it didnt happen over the dumbest ♥♥♥♥ ALL THE TIME). 

-A lack luster verity in challenges and the rewards they give you. This one is more of a subjective statement, but I feel like doing the challenges of the day become very unfun and similar because they just seem to cycle through the same ones week after week. They do add a few new ones (I want to give them flowers where they deserve it, but its not enough to bring me back or care to get it done). I also feel like they are always in the same places and never in spots or areas you dont skate. The rewards are very hit and miss. Some of the stuff is pretty rad (like the sponsored stuff), but the rest is barely worth getting in my opinion. It feels like you are collecting to just collect (which I normally love), but in this game is very unsatisfying. I do appreciate that they made opening boxes less time consuming, but It doesnt motivate me to care or continue to open them any longer.

-The map kinda sucks. I feel like San Van isnt a bad map, it does have some great skate spots, but I wish we had more verity in terrain, scenery, structures. It almost feels empty and void of real live. The cars and people are there, but they really dont add life to the city. One part of the city still isnt even open and this season (Season 2) they finally added a few challenges over there, but not enough to get people to hangout. Also when you turn off cars and people in the settings, they just go invisible, but they are still there! Vee will still say the stupid lines when you "bump" into them. I wish they just had multi maps that we could choose from instead of being trapped on this hell island called San Van.

Other random gripes: 

-The tutorial people are annoying as hell, all of them!! Also the devs missed an opportunity to make them real people in the game you meet up with. Its kinda lame to have them just pop up as a picture with a speech that I could care less about. 

-You get all these cool skating props (the one fun thing to collect), but can only place 5 down, which is lame

-The music is okay, I just listen to my spotify most of the time

-The skating its self is fun and feels good at times, but the rest of the game is not and it makes it hard to care or want to get on to play anymore.

-No Afros! (that one is a personal personal gripe), but really???

To summarize, this game has pissed me off so bad that Im done playing. Thankfully I can skate in real life, so Im going to go do that!

I never leave negative reviews on early access games, but the fact that they created a season pass at this stage opened the door for me.

Firstly, for a game that requires you to play online, the co-op systems barely work. An open party will be listed as closed to other players, so you usually have to go in and either manually invite people or change your settings back and forth, so you can actually play with your friends. Half of the time your other party members are invisible. When you can see them, the desync causes you to see any movements of party members several seconds late. You also can't see your friends on the map anymore, forcing you to teleport in a game about skating places. 

The challenges are also incredibly broken. A lot of the time, goals won't register that you're completing them, both while you're in the challenge and after you complete it. You can do a line flawlessly, and you'll have to keep doing it, hoping that the game suddenly decides to register that you're completing a certain action. There's one challenge that half the time won't allow you to complete a triple kickflip in the designated area. This isn't a skill issue. You can hit it on the way to the scoring area, but once you're actually in the highlighted area, the game won't let you get your board off the ground. Then after a challenge's completion, you'll see on the map that there's one random goal that's still missing. There's absolutely no reason that "All goals in one attempt" should be checked off but one of the other goals isn't. Also when you try to queue co-op challenges, a lot of the time it just doesn't bring your party members in with you, giving you another reason to have to keep quitting and restarting.

The physics are wildly inconsistent. You can speed into a rail head on, and sometimes it just kinda bounces you back a bit while you stay on the board. Alternatively, you can slightly graze against a rail at a shallow angle, and it might send you flying off your board at a higher speed than you were going in the first place.

The map isn't terrible, but as some other reviews say, it feels very corporate and soulless. It has a handful of good spots and parks, but there's just something about it that feels like it wasn't made with love.

The crashes are also one of this game's many mysteries. Sometimes you can hop on and play for an hour or two completely without issue. Other days you'll try to play, and you can't go ten minutes without your game deciding to close.

As I opened with, I get that this game is in early access, and it understandably still needs some polishing. A lot of these issues are things they're working on, and can be fixed relatively easily. In fact, a lot of these things didn't even happen after the game was freshly released. I don't even mind the fact that they're selling cosmetics, the game is free. But EA being EA, they prioritize selling cosmetics that don't even look good instead of ironing out fundamental issues with their game that somehow get worse every update.

This game has a lot of potential, and there's a decent amount of fun to be had in it (when it works). But unless EA learns what to focus on, this game is gonna be dead on arrival.

This game is probably the worst game they could have made as part of the skate series for a few big reasons.

Firstly, the target demographic. They made a new skate game because all the fans of the first three games wanted it. Then they switched it up and targeted children who have no idea how skateboarding works. Why? That is the most counter-intuitive choice that they could have made. And now this game has no resemblance of what the sport means to most people. Skateboarding is supposed to be difficult, requiring you to risk injury in order to do something cool. And with this "Impervatek" bs, they completely nuked that idea to the floor just to lower the age rating and get more kids to give them money through microtransactions.

Secondly, the map. The whole place just feels like a few big spots scattered throughout the most boring, repetitive map possible. I hope you enjoy skating in a city, because that's all you get. The districts are all practically identical, with no variation of decoration or features, no elevation changes, and no medium sized obstacles. Everything is just either a megaramp, or a bench. While playing this game, I haven't seen a single person after the first few weeks of the game skate anything other than their giant ramps. Every important spot is just so huge and impressive, that they all feel so artificial and samey.

Thirdly, the game being live service. Live service has to be the worst trend ever conceived by game developers. All I want out of a game, is to be able to hop on and mess around for half an hour when I have a bit of free time. What I don't want, is to be waiting 5 minutes to get into a server, just to play the same poorly playtested missions and challenges that only work half the time. The problem is, they are adding low-effort temporary content instead of permanent stuff to make the game better. I can only do one of their 4 types of missions, which get stale extremely quickly and are just recycled every time they refresh (I will give them some slack as the game is still early-access). Some more (well thought out) mission types - such as races or competitions against AI - in future updates would be appreciated.

Finally, their "early access" claims. If a game has seasons, its own version of a battle pass, and microtransactions, then this is not early access. This is a full game. The devs are just using this facade to give excuses for why the game is incomplete, yet they put their efforts onto making seasons (e.g. what they just released for Halloween). Where are dark catches and slides, where are underflips, where are other mission types and where is the replay editor from Skate 3? All we have now is just a buggy piece of crap that has no keyframes whatsoever, and can't even record at 60fps smoothly. They ruined my favourite part of 3: being able to film my tricks in a cool way. And now they put all their efforts making "seasons" as if the game is Fortnite or something. Cheers Full Circle.

However, the game does feel smoother and less buggy than Skate 3, and the art style isn't the most horrendous thing like some other people say. All of this criticism is just for now, but if they don't make some pretty drastic changes, then the game will forever be bad.

tl;dr:
they made the game for kids, not who wanted it
the map is extremely boring with only a few interesting spots
the devs add low-effort content as the game is live service
the they are adding seasons to the game, not actual permanent content

I'll be surprised if anyone is still playing this after a few months. This game is destined to be forgotten.

Personal notes: Skate. is an open world skating game set in a fictional city called San Vansterdam. This is the fourth installement in the Skate series, although they don't like to call it Skate 4. Before I start, I want to say that I grew up playing the original three Skate games and loved them. When I heard they were making a new one I was quite excited as it had been a long time since the latest game, being Skate 3 in 2010. Despite this "hype", and it being a free title I was left pretty dissapointed overall. Let's start with the good. The gameplay and skating mechanics are really well made and the main reason I love these games. It feels smooth and fluid, and hitting a solid line always feels rewarding. However, I dont credit it too much as we had these mechanics in Skate games a decade ago. I also think the multiplayer is implemented well and I appreciate rewarding teamwork. I am not the biggest fan of the artstyle personally but I can see what they were going for and It looks pretty good overall. That's about it for the good. For the bad we have quite a bit more. The gameplay loop is terrible and my biggest gripe with the game. You do these "daily" challenges which are normally the exact same day in day out. The reason you do these challenges are for rip chips/score, which you use to level up, unlock more fast travel points/challenges and customize your guy which leads me to my next point. Customization, In the old games we had so many choices for customization out the gates, In comparision to this one with barely any out the gate and all the brand items are pay-walled. Also why does a Skate game need a Battlepass and four different currencies in the first few months? Along with a store full of paid items, that shall I mention is above where you can get the free, less cool stuff. I understand microtransactions, especially being a free game but I dislike me being forced to look at it everytime. My next point is that this game, at least personally totally missed the Skate culture I knew this game for such as replacing Coach Frank with a robot voice. The fact that many game-modes are missing on launch such as Hall of Meat or S.K.A.T.E saddens me. On top of all of this, my game ran terribly. I crashed so many times regardless of the settings(RTX 4070S/AMD 5800x3D) and the friends I played with experienced similiar issues, almost to the point I wanted to give up hunting all the achievements. Achievement wise, most were pretty easy except two I listed below taking a lot of dedication. 11000 Rip score is quite the task, especially if they keep nerfing how many Rip Chips you get per daily challenge. Along with landing, not crashing with a combined hour of 4X score.  All things considered, I don't really recommend this game currently in it's state. The skating is a blast and you can certainly have some fun with your friends for free but I would rather spend my time playing any of the other decade old Skate titles instead.

Skate is an unfortunate tale of corporate greed wrapped in nostalgia. The original trilogy was beloved and defined by its authenticity, the culture, and creativity, which this entry has been revived not out of passion as the marketing deceptively says, but out of profit. This reboot of the series attempts to ride the wave of its predecessors while fundamentally misunderstanding what made them special.

The game self labels itself as an early access title, which acts as a shield meant to deflect valid criticism. Yet somehow, despite being "unfinished" it already features a battle pass, four separate in-game currencies, rotating shop offers, and micro-transactions wazoo. The presence of loot boxes and time limited bundles says everything where the priorities lie. (The only feature of this game which I have never experienced any bugs in has been the store UI, go figure)

What makes this whole thing sting even more is the contrast to the originals. The classic Skate games celebrated real skate culture, officially licensed clothing brands, professional skaters, a campaign that told your story of becoming a legend, and multiplayer built around friendly competition and creativity. This new version instead feels like a live service experiment designed to extract engagement and spending rather than evoke passion. Everything revolves around daily missions, often are the same exact spots every day, except yesterday it asked for a nose grind, today it ask for a crooked grind.

This reboot isn't just disappointing, its disheartening. I grew up playing the original trilogy on my Xbox 360, I fell in love with the secret pro tapes, the grit of every slam and scrape, and picking my favorite board brand, whether it was Baker, Alien Workshop, Krooked, all without spending a dime extra. Those games made me want to actually go outside and learn to skate.

Now it feels hollow. A series which once stood for freedom and expression of real skate culture has been turned into a monetized platform pretending to be a tribute. Until Skate and EA can find that soul again, this is a reminder of what we lost.

This game feels less like a natural evolution of the original Skate series and more like a departure from what made those titles resonate with the skateboarding community. Instead of capturing the culture, grit, and personality that defined the earlier games, this new installment often feels disconnected from actual skateboarding and the people who love it.

In the classic Skate titles, the world felt authentic. When you fell, your character got dirty, scraped up, and visibly worn down — details that added immersion and grounded the experience. The environments were gritty, full of graffiti, rough textures, and the kind of urban atmosphere skaters instantly recognize. Even the security guards added charm and unpredictability, becoming memorable parts of the gameplay loop.

In contrast, the new game feels overly polished and sanitized. The world is clean to the point of feeling artificial, and it lacks the personality and edge that defined the earlier entries. One of the biggest disappointments is the absence of real skate brands. Iconic companies like Element, Zero, Blind, Baker, and many others helped players feel connected to the culture. Seeing a board you actually owned appear in‑game created a sense of identity and authenticity. Now, the equipment feels generic — almost like skating on department‑store boards with no real-world relevance.

The challenges also fall short. They’re repetitive, uninspired, and rarely offer anything that feels genuinely fun or rewarding. Without meaningful progression, recognizable brands, or a world that reflects real skate culture, it becomes difficult to feel invested. Instead of celebrating the community, the game often comes across as a monetized product focused more on cosmetic sales than on delivering an experience skaters can relate to.

Overall, it’s disappointing to see a series that once captured the heart of skateboarding shift toward something that feels more like a cash grab than a love letter to the culture. There’s potential here, but right now, it lacks the authenticity, attitude, and soul that made the original Skate games so memorable.

[h3] Gameplay: [/h3] 
The skating elements are directly ripped from skate 3 for the most part. Some missing moves but I like the fluidity of the gameplay part of this game. As much as you can hate on every other part of the game, if they did not nail this it would have been dead on arrival. They did improve the system in this game, and the prop overhaul for this game made me actually use it, unlike skate 3's. I don't think it's something to brag about though and put moves that were in skate 3 in the game's road map. That's like saying a store change is a major feature.

[h3] Early Access: [/h3] 
I feel this game isn't gonna survive after Early Access. I understand the point for indie games, but when you send out an incomplete game just to say it's Early Access doesn't mean it is excused for missing features from previous entries. This is a triple a game and they could have easily funded and just did a open beta, close for a year and update the game.

[h3] Linux Support: [/h3] 
I wish this game worked on the steam deck. Just wanted to add this in here that it doesn't like Linux, I guess the anticheat? I geniuely do not understand.

[h3] Conclusion: [/h3] 
Fun game, terrible decisions. It is still a skate game and its on Steam. Again the thing you can compare this to is Halo Infinite. Free game that kills itself with greed, but overall a good game underneath all of the crud that's thrown on it. I just finished the 100% achievement for it today, hopefully when I come back something is added, but this game got bland after the 4th hour in or so.

At the end of the day it is still free, so pick it up and ♥♥♥♥ around for a bit.
